subject.title: exec auto-reviewer re-bills a fresh model completion for every byte-identical repeated exec

question: May OpenClaw reuse model-backed exec reviewer decisions for byte-identical exec requests, and should that cache be limited to one reviewer/run keyed by the full reviewed input?
rationale: The source-reproducible bug is narrow, but caching an approval reviewer result changes when a later exec bypasses a fresh model review, so the cache lifetime, key shape, and plugin-helper scope need maintainer intent.

options.title: Approve full-input per-run memo
options.body: Cache parsed reviewer decisions only inside the shared reviewer instance, keyed by the full reviewed input or prompt, and do not persist or convert them to durable approvals.

options.title: Memoize allow-once only
options.body: Cache only low-risk allow-once results and keep ask, error, and timeout decisions uncached for a narrower behavior change with smaller savings.

options.title: Keep fresh review semantics
options.body: Accept repeated model cost to preserve one-request-one-review behavior until stronger security or live billing evidence justifies changing the approval boundary.

recommendation.title: Approve full-input per-run memo
recommendation.body: Cache parsed reviewer decisions only inside the shared reviewer instance, keyed by the full reviewed input or prompt, and do not persist or convert them to durable approvals.
